OBJECTIVE 
I am an AI & DS student with a strong interest in technology, seeking an internship opportunity to apply analytical thinking, 
programming skills, and creativity to real-world projects while contributing to innovative teams through software development 
and technology-driven solutions for environmental and business growth. 
EXPERIENCE

consistency and load performance. 
• Applied cloud computing fundamentals to deploy and test web components in a live server environment under senior 
developer guidance. 
• Collaborated in technical design discussions, contributing implementation ideas adopted into the final deployment plan. 
Intern — EDU TANTR                                                                                                                                                       Dec 2025 
• Analyzed real-world datasets using Python-based data science workflows, improving data quality through structured 
cleaning and preprocessing. 
• Implemented analytical and problem-solving techniques across assigned tasks, delivering results within a collaborative, 
deadline-driven environment. 
• Strengthened data science and critical-thinking skills through hands-on training in industry-standard workflows and best 
practices. 
PROJECTS 
AI Sign Language Translation Platform 
Developed an AI-based sign language translator supporting real-time webcam, image, and video recognition. Built an interactive 
dashboard for dataset management, model training, and prediction visualization, streamlining the ML workflow end-to-end. 
Optimized UI/UX and deployed a responsive web application, improving accessibility of digital communication for hearing-
impaired users. 
Tree Plantation & Carbon Reduction Calculator 
Engineered a web-based carbon footprint calculator estimating CO2 emissions and recommending tree-planting offsets. Built an 
interactive dashboard with real-time calculations and data visualizations, delivering personalized sustainability insights. 
Designed a responsive, user-friendly interface to promote environmental awareness and support eco-friendly decision-making.

company_insights.title: TCS Recruitment Process & Coding Round Pattern
company_insights.content: TCS conducts its recruitment primarily through TCS NQT (National Qualifier Test). The process has 2 main sections: 1. Cognitive Assessment (Quantitative Aptitude, Verbal Ability, Reasoning Ability). 2. Programming Assessment (Coding questions in C/C++/Java/Python/Perl). The programming section features one basic logic problem and one advanced problem (usually array/string manipulation or dynamic programming). After clearing NQT, there are Technical, Managerial, and HR interviews. In Technical rounds, candidates are grilled on OOPs, DBMS, SQL joins, and basic data structures.

company_insights.title: Google SWE Interview Structure & Topics
company_insights.content: Google SWE interviews focus heavily on algorithms, data structures, and problem-solving ability. Typically involves 1 phone screen followed by 4-5 virtual onsites. Topics highly prioritized include graphs (BFS/DFS, Dijkstra's), trees (binary trees, BST, trie), dynamic programming, recursion, hash tables, and system design (for mid/senior level). Interviewers evaluate you on four categories: Cognitive Ability, Role-Related Knowledge (RRK), Leadership/Googliness, and Coding. Clean, optimal, and bug-free code is expected.

company_insights.title: Amazon Data Scientist Interview & Leadership Principles
company_insights.content: Amazon Data Scientist interviews evaluate technical depth in Machine Learning, coding, case study analysis, and alignment with Leadership Principles. The process consists of a phone screen with ML case study and coding, followed by 5 onsite loops. Expect coding questions in SQL (joins, window functions) and Python (algorithms or data processing). The ML portion focuses heavily on supervised/unsupervised algorithms, evaluation metrics (ROC-AUC, F1-score), feature engineering, and deep learning. Every response in behavioral questions must incorporate Amazon's Leadership Principles (like Customer Obsession and Bias for Action).

company_insights.title: Infosys HackWithInfy and InfyTQ Channels
company_insights.content: Infosys recruits through three main tracks: InfyTQ certification exam, HackWithInfy coding competition, and standard on-campus drives. HackWithInfy is a coding competition with two rounds testing competitive programming skills. InfyTQ focuses on Python, Database Management Systems (DBMS), and OOPs. The technical interview following InfyTQ certification tests projects mentioned on the resume, database concepts, basic arrays/strings programs, and basic web technologies (HTML/CSS/JS).

company_insights.title: Wipro Elite National Talent Hunt (NLTH) Pattern
company_insights.content: Wipro NLTH consists of three sections: 1. Quantitative, Logical, and Verbal English aptitude. 2. Coding (2 programs of medium difficulty in C/C++/Java/Python). 3. Written English Test (Essay writing). In the technical interview, candidates are commonly asked to write basic programs like Fibonacci series, prime check, palindrome, or factorial. Questions on relational databases, keys (primary, foreign), and basic computer networks are highly common.

company_insights.title: TCS Frequently Asked Technical Questions
company_insights.content:
Q1: What is the difference between Method Overloading and Method Overriding?
Q2: Write a query to find the second highest salary from an Employee table.
Q3: What are the different types of joins in SQL?
Q4: Explain the SDLC waterfall model vs Agile.
Q5: What is a pointer and how is memory managed in C++?

company_insights.title: Google SWE Commonly Asked Coding Questions
company_insights.content:
Q1: Design a search autocomplete system (System Design).
Q2: Find the longest path in a directed acyclic graph.
Q3: Given a binary tree, find the maximum path sum between two nodes.
Q4: Implement a rate limiter using token bucket or sliding window algorithm.
Q5: Find the median of two sorted arrays of different sizes in O(log(min(m, n))) time.

company_insights.title: Amazon DS Core ML and SQL Questions
company_insights.content:
Q1: Explain bias-variance tradeoff in Machine Learning.
Q2: Write a SQL query using window functions to find the top 3 selling products per category.
Q3: How would you deal with imbalanced datasets in predictive modeling?
Q4: Describe how you would set up an A/B test for a new checkout page UI.
Q5: What is the mathematical explanation of Gradient Descent?

company_insights.title: Infosys Common Technical Qs
company_insights.content:
Q1: Explain the pillars of Object Oriented Programming.
Q2: Write a program to reverse a string without using built-in methods.
Q3: What is the difference between primary key, unique key, and candidate key?
Q4: Explain the difference between GET and POST HTTP requests.
Q5: What is normalization and why do we use it in DBMS?

company_insights.title: Wipro Technical Coding Questions
company_insights.content:
Q1: How do you check if a linked list contains a cycle?
Q2: What is the difference between compiler and interpreter?
Q3: Write a program to check if two strings are anagrams of each other.
Q4: What is the use of 'final' keyword in Java?
Q5: Write a SQL query to delete duplicate rows from a table.
